items.case: A single shared secret powers three unrelated services.
items.answer: Create scoped workload identities, rotate secrets under change approval and verify dependent requests.
items.evidence: Service-to-resource grant matrix and successful rotation checks.
items.pitfall: Shared credentials enlarge the blast radius.

items.case: Authentication succeeds but a data-access event is absent.
items.answer: Check application authorization and resource logs separately; identify coverage gaps before inferring what data was accessed.
items.evidence: Sign-in and resource audit fields with correlation IDs.
items.pitfall: Login success does not prove data retrieval.

items.case: A staff analyst should access reports only for their assigned region.
items.answer: Apply role permissions plus trusted region attributes at the server and test own-region access against out-of-region denial.
items.evidence: Policy decision matrix and both test outcomes.
items.pitfall: A broad role alone cannot enforce regional restrictions.

items.case: A break-glass identity is used during an outage.
items.answer: Require a documented emergency, restricted duration, detailed audit and retrospective approval with prompt privilege removal.
items.evidence: Emergency ticket, activation/expiry and reviewer signoff.
items.pitfall: Emergency privilege must not become permanent.

items.case: A service identity is in an unrelated privileged group.
items.answer: Inspect expected versus effective group membership, assess dependencies, remove excess access under approval and retest.
items.evidence: id output, permission matrix and functional verification.
items.pitfall: A functioning service can still be overprivileged.

items.case: Host load is high while CPU use remains low.
items.answer: Investigate blocked processes, I/O wait and storage latency; load measures runnable or uninterruptible tasks, not CPU percentage alone.
items.evidence: Process state, disk latency and timed baseline.
items.pitfall: High load is not always CPU saturation.

items.case: A security patch may restart a shared Linux service.
items.answer: Stage the update, review dependencies, plan downtime and rollback, install in authorized window and verify service behavior.
items.evidence: Version/advisory, test outcomes, change approval and post-patch logs.
items.pitfall: Successful package installation alone does not prove recovery.

items.case: A scheduled reporting task runs with unnecessary root privilege.
items.answer: Inspect job owner, necessary filesystem access and logs; change to a limited account and verify jobs through approved testing.
items.evidence: Crontab or timer definition, account grants and result evidence.
items.pitfall: Automation convenience doesn't justify excess privilege.

items.case: A server drifts from its approved access baseline.
items.answer: Compare exact effective settings against a versioned benchmark, determine valid exceptions and remediate only approved deviations.
items.evidence: Baseline revision, config difference, owner and revalidation.
items.pitfall: A generic hardening checklist is not an asset-specific risk assessment.

items.case: An untrusted display name appears in an HTML attribute.
items.answer: Use output encoding appropriate to the attribute and safe templating; verify harmless special characters render as data.
items.evidence: Context-specific before/after render and safe output test.
items.pitfall: HTML text encoding is not universally correct in attributes or script contexts.

items.case: A website uses ambient session cookies for state-changing requests.
items.answer: Use appropriate anti-CSRF tokens or origin validation, with SameSite as additional defense; verify legitimate same-origin requests.
items.evidence: Expected valid and disallowed synthetic state-change tests.
items.pitfall: SameSite alone may not cover every application context.

items.case: A team portal accepts files from authenticated users.
items.answer: Enforce type and size constraints, segregated non-executable storage, content checks and authorized retrieval.
items.evidence: Allowed/rejected sample cases and storage isolation design.
items.pitfall: Trusted login or filename extension does not make an upload safe.

items.case: A valid session requests a record owned by a different tenant.
items.answer: Enforce per-request tenant/object authorization at the server and validate denied foreign access and permitted owner use.
items.evidence: Principal, tenant, object and policy decision for two synthetic cases.
items.pitfall: Authentication is not authorization to arbitrary records.

items.case: A site emits a CSP header with broadly permissive script rules.
items.answer: Review actual directives and trusted script sources, adjust policy with testing and monitor violations.
items.evidence: Header snapshot, safe browser check and functional regression evidence.
items.pitfall: Presence of a header is not proof of effective protection.

items.case: A cloud database is reachable from a public application subnet that doesn't need it.
items.answer: Narrow effective network policies to required service sources and verify allowed and denied connections.
items.evidence: Diagram, rule evaluation and controlled reachability tests.
items.pitfall: A private address does not independently ensure isolation.

items.case: Application credentials appear in a public deployment configuration.
items.answer: Treat them as exposed, rotate through approved secret management, scope access and validate consumers.
items.evidence: Revocation record, current grants and successful dependent transaction.
items.pitfall: Removing published text does not revoke leaked secrets.

items.case: A storage permission changes without a corresponding audit event.
items.answer: Check audit capture configuration, retention and source availability; report visibility limitations without inventing events.
items.evidence: Policy revision time, audit settings and corroborating change record.
items.pitfall: Absence of a log isn't proof of no activity.

items.case: A broad infrastructure policy change lacks peer review.
items.answer: Require approved ownership, plan/diff, least-privilege adjustment, rollback and post-change testing.
items.evidence: Change ticket, diff and positive/negative access outcomes.
items.pitfall: A successfully applied change may still be unsafe.

items.case: An object policy was public but access logs are unavailable.
items.answer: Report confirmed exposure configuration, unknown actual readership, containment, evidence limitations and follow-up.
items.evidence: Effective policy, time range and clear distinction between exposure and access.
items.pitfall: Public accessibility is not confirmed data exfiltration.

items.case: A portal accepts external files for internal review.
items.answer: Map uploader, processing engine, storage, staff reader and trust boundaries; prioritize realistic failure paths.
items.evidence: Data-flow diagram with assumptions and testable security controls.
items.pitfall: A hypothetical weakness isn't a verified finding.
